title: DDIL geospatial data logistics: versioned delta-sync and prioritized distribution of basemaps, 3D terrain and overlays across TAK Server federations and NGC2 edge nodes
problem: Tactical units still pre-load basemaps and 3D terrain by hand and lose overlay consistency across devices and federated servers when links drop, because no fielded, vendor-neutral service versions, prioritizes and delta-syncs geospatial artifacts (tiles, 3D Tiles, overlays) across TAK Server federations and NGC2 hub/spoke edge nodes under bandwidth budgets.

user.exact_role: Brigade/battalion geospatial engineer (12Y) and TAK Server administrator (S6 section) who build and distribute map/terrain packages; team leaders who load devices before missions; division data-layer operators on NGC2 nodes
user.echelon: battalion/brigade primary; team/platoon as consumers; division as source
organization_examples: Army BCT S2 geospatial cell and S6 (e.g., 4ID and 25ID NGC2 prototype divisions)
DHS/CBP TAK users (unclassified first customer candidate)
Allied TAK adopters (NATO members, Australia) and Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN units

current_workflow: Geospatial cell pulls imagery, elevation and OWT/3D terrain from enterprise sources (NGA/AGC, PEO STRI OWT, commercial) while on a good link and builds MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ/3D-tile packages.
Packages are sideloaded to end-user devices by hand (USB/'sneakernet') or pushed as TAK mission packages/data-sync missions before the mission; large 3D terrain is rarely refreshed once units move.

During operations, overlays (graphics, routes, targets) are edited on multiple ATAK/WinTAK/TAKX clients and on several TAK Servers; changes propagate via server data sync and federation when links are up.
When links drop, edits diverge; on reconnection the picture is reconciled by whole-object replay or overwritten, and staff manually decide which version is current.
Bulk resync after outages competes with voice, PLI and video for SATCOM/MANET capacity; there is no content-aware prioritization of what reaches the edge first.
Coalition partners exchange a translated subset of the picture (e.g., ASCA between TAK, SitaWare, FC BISA) with liaison officers filling gaps.
current_solution: TAK Server data sync ('missions'), mission packages and server-to-server federation (whole-object replication, not delta- or bandwidth-optimized - RECALL, not re-verified this session, MEDIUM); Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (CRDT peer-to-peer sync of CoT/objects without a server, company-reported USSOCOM use); Immersive Wisdom's low/no-bandwidth collaboration platform (DoD-wide sole-source ordering contract); Anduril Lattice / Palantir edge-to-cloud mesh inside the NGC2 data layer for the two prototype divisions; Reveal Farsight for edge-generated 3D terrain; manual packaging and sideloading by geospatial cells.
failure: The failure is at TRANSPORT/DISSEMINATE between the source of geospatial truth (server or division node) and the disconnected edge device: (1) no delta encoding or content-addressing for tiles/3D Tiles/overlays, so reconnection replays whole objects; (2) no cross-server, cross-federation versioning of the picture, so divergent overlay edits are resolved by hand; (3) no bandwidth-budgeted prioritization, so terrain/basemap refreshes either saturate the link or never happen; (4) NGC2's data mesh explicitly does not yet extend to tactical echelons (UDRA RFI), leaving battalion-and-below on the TAK/mission-package model.

evidence.claim: PM Mission Command's 'Operational Mission Command Suite' notice requires the TAK solution to support on-prem, hybrid and cloud data services integrated via DDIL-robust protocols and architectures, alongside a common data model, data fabric and data catalog - i.e., DDIL-tolerant TAK data services are a stated Army requirement, not a solved feature.
evidence.source_title: Operational Mission Command Suite (SAM.gov notice; captured in evidence sweep E02-F8)
evidence.pub_date: unknown (2025-2026 inferred; primary page blocked by proxy)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army's Unified Data Reference Architecture RFI states domain data products will be produced at lower echelons 'by exception only' until lessons learned can extend the data mesh toward tactical units - an explicit admission that tactical-echelon data distribution/mesh is unsolved.
evidence.source_title: Unified Data Reference Architecture RFI (SAM.gov; evidence sweep E02-F7)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army describes NGC2 as an edge-to-cloud data architecture intended to keep working over intermittent links and awarded Anduril a $99.6M, 11-month prototype OTA (July 2025) - proof the Army treats data availability under DDIL as a priority problem; prototype award, not deployment.
evidence.source_title: Army announces Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) prototype award
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Ivy Sting 4 (early 2026) deliberately tested C2 of maneuver from division to battalion under 'denied network conditions', showing that DDIL data continuity is an explicit NGC2 test objective; outcomes for map/overlay sync are not public.
evidence.source_title: CPE C2IN post on Ivy Sting 4 (evidence sweep E03-F9)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Air Force awarded Immersive Wisdom a DoD-wide five-year sole-source ordering contract (ceiling $25M through GFY2029) for TRL-9 no-/low-bandwidth collaboration software, followed by a STRATFI with matching funds from three DoD commands (Nov 2024) - repeat buying of low-bandwidth shared-picture software; ceiling is not revenue and obligations are undisclosed.
evidence.source_title: SOF Week 2024: Immersive Wisdom awarded DoD-wide five-year sole-source $25MM ordering contract (PR Newswire)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: One World Terrain moved from a 2019-2024 support/Phase 4 arrangement to a production OTA with Vantor (ceiling up to $217M, Feb 2026), and OWT 3D terrain is intended for mission planning/rehearsal including ATAK use - the volume of 3D data that must reach edge devices is growing; ceiling, not obligations.
evidence.source_title: Army Awards Vantor $217 Million Contract To Transition One World Terrain To Production (Defense Daily) / BusinessWire release
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: At least four partial solutions coexist without a vendor-neutral geospatial delta-sync layer: TAK Server data sync/federation (government), Ditto Edge Sync plugin for ATAK (CRDT P2P object sync, company-reported USSOCOM use, ~$136M raised), Immersive Wisdom (low-bandwidth collaboration), and Reveal Farsight (edge-generated 3D terrain, $33.6M STRATFI). None is documented to delta-sync basemaps/3D Tiles with bandwidth-budgeted prioritization across federations.
evidence.source_title: Ditto press release on ABMS IDIQ award; company product pages (compiled in companies/B03.json, B02.json, B07.json)
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Bold Quest 2025 (Joint Staff J6 exercise) coalition SA exchange between TAK, SitaWare and FC BISA was constrained by network challenges during the short deployment window - reported by a vendor but describing a government exercise.
evidence.source_title: Systematic experts support coalition forces during Bold Quest 2025
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Ukraine's cloud-hosted Delta situational-awareness system depends on Starlink and degrades where connectivity is limited, and Delta and Kropyva are 'not fully integrated' - a fielded-war illustration that a shared geospatial picture fails without connection-tolerant sync.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Manual pre-loading and USB/mission-package distribution of map tiles and terrain remains standard practice in TAK units. NOT VERIFIED THIS SESSION: the web-search quota was exhausted before a primary source (TAK user docs, unit SOP, after-action report) could be captured; treat as RECALL.
evidence.source_title: TAK.gov products page (does not itself document the workaround)
evidence.label: HYPOTHESIS

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: The overlay/object-sync half is being attacked by Ditto (general-purpose CRDT sync SDK with an ATAK plugin) and Immersive Wisdom (collaboration UI), and the government's own TAK Server already ships data sync and federation for free, so venture-backed teams see a feature, not a product. The basemap/3D-terrain half is unglamorous data logistics: it needs radios and a field exercise to demonstrate, the buyers (TPC, PM MC, PEO STRI OWT, AGC, NGC2 data-layer prime) are fragmented so nobody owns end-to-end 'get the right terrain to the right device under a bandwidth budget', and the NGC2 primes (Anduril/Palantir) are expected to handle transport inside their data layer. Result: everybody assumes someone else owns it and the geospatial cells keep sneakernetting.
technical_wedge: A content-addressed, priority-aware sync engine for geospatial artifacts - raster/vector tiles (MBTiles/GeoPackage), 3D Tiles/OWT terrain, and overlays modeled as CRDT documents - exposed as (a) a TAK Server plugin / federation peer that computes per-client deltas against a versioned manifest and schedules transfers under a per-link bandwidth budget with mission-area priority (AO polygon, echelon, time-to-mission), and (b) an ATAK/TAKX client plugin that requests only missing chunks and merges overlay edits conflict-free on reconnection. Later: an NGC2-side adapter so division nodes publish versioned terrain/overlay data products consumable by TAK federations and coalition servers.

mvp.what: Two TAK Servers (federated) and 8-10 ATAK-CIV devices on a lab MANET/Wi-Fi with a WAN emulator (loss, 10-64 kbit/s, outages); a sync service that versions and delta-distributes an open basemap, a Cesium-ion/OSM-derived 3D-tile terrain set and shared overlays.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Measured bytes-to-converge and time-to-converge versus native TAK data sync/mission packages across scripted outage patterns; prioritized delivery of the mission-area terrain first; zero-manual-merge overlay convergence after partitions; a pre-mission 'what is stale on this device' report.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: A 5-10x reduction in bytes to converge after outages, deterministic conflict-free overlay merge, and that a geospatial NCO can replace USB loading with a policy ('keep AO tiles fresh within 24h') - plus that it runs as an unmodified-TAK-Server plugin so TPC/PM MC do not have to change the baseline.

data_requirement.what: Open basemaps and terrain (OSM, USGS 3DEP, Copernicus DEM, Cesium ion / OSM Buildings 3D Tiles), synthetic overlays and scripted link profiles; later CUI exercise data via a sponsor. No classified data needed for the MVP; OWT itself is government-furnished and not needed to prove the logistics layer.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes for the MVP (all open/commercial). OWT/TAK-MIL/TAK-GOV builds require sponsor access and are distribution-controlled; a non-U.S.-person founder's access to TAK-GOV/MIL and OWT needs counsel and sponsor approval.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; the German founder counts only after obtaining permanent residency, and the Indonesian founder's equity must be structured so the U.S.-person threshold holds (needs counsel; not a legal judgment). xTech tracks are mostly limited to eligible small businesses, though xTechInternational is open to foreign firms. DIU CSO has no small-business ownership rule but FOCI/export review applies. TAK-GOV/MIL builds and OWT access are distribution-controlled; a non-U.S.-person founder's access requires sponsor and export-control review.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes for NGC2 divisions: Anduril's Lattice Mesh and Palantir's edge stack already move data hub-to-spoke and they lead the common data layer baseline; TPC could add delta/priority sync to TAK Server in a release. Ditto could extend its ATAK plugin to tiles/3D Tiles with modest effort.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only as the neutral, TAK-native layer that works across TAK federations, non-NGC2 units (SOF, USMC, DHS, allies) and both NGC2 primes - a position the primes have no incentive to fill and TPC is slow to fill (INFERENCE). If the value is confined to NGC2 divisions, reject: the primes will absorb it. The defensible framing is 'geospatial artifact logistics under bandwidth budgets' (tiles/3D terrain/overlays as versioned data products), which is narrower and more specialized than Ditto's general sync SDK.

regulatory_burden.explanation: MVP on ATAK-CIV and open data is unrestricted. TAK-GOV/MIL builds are distribution-controlled; encryption in the product is typically EAR 5D002 with License Exception ENC (RECALL, verify); OWT data and exercise data are CUI or controlled; military-specific TAK plugins may raise ITAR questions (USML Category XI software) that need counsel. An ATO or TPC plugin approval is required for fielding.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a U.S. person) may be unable to access TAK-GOV/MIL builds, OWT data, CUI exercise data or ITAR-controlled technical data without authorization; the company may need a deemed-export plan, role segregation, and possibly a FOCI mitigation structure. SBIR eligibility hinges on the U.S.-person ownership majority. These are constraints to work through with export-control and immigration counsel, not legal conclusions.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Offline-first, bandwidth-budgeted distribution of map tiles, 3D terrain and shared overlays maps to wildfire/incident management, search and rescue, border and maritime agencies, mining/energy field ops and humanitarian mapping (all TAK or ATAK-CIV adjacent). The commercial market is real but fragmented and price-sensitive; Ditto shows the generic-sync version sells commercially (airlines, retail), while the geospatial-specific version is narrower.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility comes from being the TPC-listed/accredited plugin that units already run across federations, the artifact-aware scheduling heuristics tuned on real link telemetry, and adapters into OWT/NGC2/coalition servers. The core idea (CRDT + content-addressed delta sync) is not patentable moat; speed to deployment footprint and TPC/PM MC relationships are.

why_now: Three changes since 2023: (1) NGC2 (2025-2026) reframed Army C2 as an edge-to-cloud data layer with DDIL as a test objective (Ivy Sting 4, PC-C6) and the UDRA RFI admits the mesh stops above tactical echelons; (2) One World Terrain went to production (Feb 2026) and SBMC/TAK-compatible soldier devices multiply the 3D data that must reach the edge; (3) WinTAK sunset and TAKX (2026) reopen the plugin ecosystem, and CRDT/content-addressed sync tech (Ditto, IPFS-style chunking) is now mature enough to run on soldier devices. Also, SBIR/STTR was reauthorized in 2026 after the 2025 lapse, reopening the non-dilutive path.
killer_risk: The problem may already be 'good enough' solved by free and funded incumbents: TAK Server data sync/federation for overlays plus Ditto's ATAK Edge Sync plugin (well-capitalized, company-claimed SOF use) cover the object-sync half, and NGC2 primes will be assumed to own transport for the division half - leaving a startup with only the basemap/3D-terrain logistics sliver, whose demand this session could not verify with a primary source (the manual-USB workaround remains a hypothesis) and which buyers may treat as a feature TPC should ship.

allied_extension: Yes, materially more compelling. Allied and coalition TAK users (NATO members, Australia, DHS-like agencies) sit outside NGC2 and will never be served by Anduril/Palantir's division data layer, and coalition exercises (Bold Quest 2025) show network-limited SA exchange across TAK/SitaWare/FC BISA. The German founder can pursue NATO DIANA and Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN-adjacent channels (D-LBO re-sequenced after a failed system test in Nov 2025, EUR 11.5bn programme), where an unclassified, TAK-native geospatial sync layer is a plausible pilot. Caveats: EU-only instruments (EDF) exclude third-country-controlled entities, allied TAK variants and ITAR flow-down complicate a single product, and allied budgets for TAK plugins are small.
